# GitHub

What GitHub holds for Planton's access to this repository.

## Planton's GitHub App on the `whysosuresh` account

- **App:** "Planton AI", developed by plantonhq. It is Planton production's own App; the App's key is Planton's, and nothing of it lives in this repository.
- **Installation:** 178170335, installed on the personal account `whysosuresh` on 2026-11-03. Recorded as `Connection.GithubConnection.github-whysosuresh`.
- **Repository access:** "Only select repositories", with one repository: `whysosuresh/whysosuresh.com`. The first install landed on "All repositories" and was narrowed the same minute. On GitHub this is Settings, Applications, Installed GitHub Apps, Planton AI, Repository access.
- **Permissions it asks for:** read access to metadata; read and write access to actions, checks, code, deployments, pull requests and repository hooks.

**Changing it.** Adding a repository is a change on GitHub. The proof is `planton connect github list-repos github-whysosuresh --instance planton.ai --org why-so-suresh`, and the change is recorded here the same day. Uninstalling the App cuts Planton off. A new installation has a new id, so the connection file changes with it.
